html:
SMTO-SKL-0125 — Slack couldn't find that channel

GUID: 37bbb718-bee5-522d-bc3d-6840da962e8f
Slug: slack-channel-not-found
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: slack

What happened

  • Slack says the channel SMTO asked for doesn't exist or can't be seen by your connected Slack account. Nothing was read or changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the Agent to list your Slack conversations and pick the channel from that list. SMTO needs the channel's exact Slack ID; a channel name alone isn't enough.
  2. If the channel is private, make sure the connected Slack account or app is a member of it in Slack. Slack hides private channels from accounts that aren't in them, so they look missing.
  3. If you have more than one Slack connection, check you're using the one for the right workspace. A channel in one workspace can't be found through another workspace's connection.
  4. Ask the Agent for your request again using the channel from the list. Slack didn't act on the first request, so repeating it with the right channel is safe.

What success looks like

  • The Agent finds the channel and completes your request.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the channel name, to your Slack workspace admin. Don't guess or type in channel IDs by hand.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Slack returned channel_not_found for the supplied channel_id under the selected workspace principal.

What this means

  • Slack returns the channel_not_found API reason. The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Slack returns the channel_not_found API reason.

How to diagnose it

  • Verify exact channel_id and visibility under the selected workspace/principal.

How to fix it

  • Resolve an accessible exact channel_id with slack.conversations (or slack.conversation) under the intended workspace_ref; display names never authorize writes, and private conversations are invisible to non-member principals.
  • Discover an accessible exact channel_id with slack.conversations; display names do not authorize mutations.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • Discovery or an authorized read resolves the intended accessible channel.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
